newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Yield Spreads-Narrow slightly pre-FOMC.
newsitem.headline: Australia Yield Spreads-Narrow slightly pre-FOMC.

text.p: Australian bonds spreads finished slightly narrower against other dollar-bloc countries as the market kept to itself ahead of the U.S. FOMC meeting today and key wages data later this week.

After opening a couple of points softer, some afternoon buying saw bonds move back to be roughly square on the day, leaving spreads slightly narrower as the U.S. Treasury market had softened overnight.
The FOMC is the major event for markets, which are fairly evenly divided over the prospects for another hike in U.S. rates to follow the move after the March meeting.
Traders said given the mixed expectations it was difficult to know exactly how Treasuries would react to the FOMC outcome.
In turn, apart from local bonds moving the same direction as Treasuries, it was hard to know just how spreads would react, especially as the local market had key wages data to follow.
Data on enterprise bargaining agreements is released on Wednesday and final average weekly ordinary time earnings (AWOTE) is due on Thursday.
"Well if they don't tighten, certainly people are going to be closely looking at the wages data, and if they do, well I think it reduces the impact of the wages data," one trader said.

Any volatility this week should be centred around the short end, with the local short end generally expected to rally if the U.S. does not tighten and the wages data are well behaved, as that would put a local easing back on the agenda, traders said.
